analysis.title: #GLOBALMARKETS WEEKLY WRAP-UP, October 03, 2026
key_insights: US equities ended the week mixed: Nasdaq and S&P Mid Cap 400 rose, Dow and S&P 500 fell. Weak September payrolls cut expectations for an October Fed hike, while high Treasury yields, volatile oil and US-Iran tensions weighed on sentiment.
September nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 vs 90,000 expected. Prior months were revised down by 60,000 and unemployment rose to 4.2% vs 4.1% expected. Average hourly earnings were 3.0% vs 3.1% expected.

Futures-implied odds of an October Fed hike fell to 15% from almost 75% a week earlier, per one cited source. Another cited source puts the chance of no October hike at 71%, up from 35% a week earlier. The Fed raised rates a quarter point last month.

Inflation stayed sticky: headline PCE 3.4% annually and core PCE 3.0%. Historical PCE year-over-year figures were revised down in the 2026 annual update because of BEA methodology changes. Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2%, with underlying private demand up 4.6%.

ISM manufacturing PMI was 54.5, a ninth straight month of growth, but its prices index surged to 77.9, signalling renewed cost pressure. Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q3 fell to 3.7% from 5.0% on September 25.

Stocks, bonds and oil broke from the 'Iran War regime' pattern midweek: oil rose, stocks were flat and bonds fell. Brent was above $102 late Friday with no sign of an off-ramp in Iran and tanker attacks escalating through the week. One chart note says oil fell below $90 on Friday on reports Europe may release diesel and crude reserves, which conflicts with the Brent figure.

G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel stocks in response to Trump's threatened US ban on diesel exports. The release is expected to pressure refining cracks short term while crude trades on Hormuz news, including a report of renewed Saudi-Houthi hostilities.

Market breadth is weak under a range-bound S&P 500 near record highs. New lows outpace new highs, fewer than half of S&P 500 members trade above their 200-day moving averages, and 75% of S&P 500 stocks were down this month per a FactSet heatmap.

The market is split between AI winners and everything else. Accenture rose about 20% on Q4 results and a strong fiscal 2027 outlook (EPS $3.29 vs $3.18 expected, margins up from 11.6% to 15.3%). Synopsys rose 12% on an Amazon cloud agreement worth over $1B and an OpenAI partnership. Nike is down more than 40% on the year after falling revenue and layoff plans, and is about 80% below its peak at a 13-year low of $35.
Tech outperformed and Financials lagged. Mag7 beat the S&P 493. Momentum rebounded sharply. Memory stocks recovered from a weak Monday open before stalling.

NVDA hit a record high on the way to a $6T market cap. Its forward P/E fell to 17x, the lowest in five years. Reported China approvals for Nvidia's newest high-end chip (ByteDance, Alibaba) are a possible catalyst.
Semiconductor free cash flow has passed $400B while hyperscaler cash flow has turned negative. Micron produced $93B of profit in three quarters of 2026 vs $59B over nearly a decade.

Anthropic's IPO prospectus leaked to Reuters: 2025 net loss of $42B, operating loss over $8B, $518B of future cloud and infrastructure commitments (reportedly 80% non-cancelable), 2025 revenue of $4.6B (12x growth), and about 25% of revenue from two customers. A $2T valuation equals 435x 2025 sales, 31x the July 2026 annualized run rate of $65B, and 10x the 2028 revenue forecast of $200B. The IPO could slip until after the November midterms.
OpenAI is raising $30B at a $1.2T valuation, about 17x its revenue run rate.

The Treasury curve rose on the week except the 2-year, and 2s30s steepened sharply. The 30-year yield is 5.6%. The longest-duration Treasury ETF is down 67% from its March 2020 peak. The US bond market has been in drawdown for 74 months, the longest on record. Short positions in Treasuries are surging.

Credit is joining the bond market's repricing. US high-yield spreads widened about 39bps on the week to about 312bps. CCC spreads hit 1,007bps, the first time above 1,000bps since March 2023. Investment-grade spreads widened more modestly but decoupled from stocks.

France is the focus of European stress. The 10-year OAT yield reached about 4.92-4.95%, the highest in roughly two decades, and the spread over Bunds passed 140bps, the widest since the 2012 euro crisis. The French-Swiss 10-year spread is at a record. France now pays more than Italy, and the BTP-Bund spread has begun to widen, which Goldman reads as the market pricing European sovereign risk rather than only French fiscal risk. The deficit is expected at 5.5% of GDP. Prediction markets show a 46% chance Le Pen wins the next French presidential election.

The euro fell, lifting the Bloomberg dollar index for a third straight week to above its 18-month range. DXY is at its highest since April 2025. USD/JPY stalled near 158 after a hotter Tokyo CPI revived talk of another BoJ move, and EUR/JPY hit a ten-month low.
Gold spiked briefly after payrolls then faded to the week's lows, with $4,200 seen as support. Monday saw a nearly 4% gold selloff.

Bitcoin rose above $87,000, its highest since September 23, then gave back gains Friday afternoon as real yields spiked. Cumulative Bitcoin ETF flows remain about $5B short of recovering the outflow hole since the October 10 peak.

Midterm politics: Polymarket gives Democrats 63% for the Senate and 93% for the House. Trump's 37% approval is the lowest of any president before a midterm in data back to 1990. An AP-NORC poll found 69% say the Iran war was not worth fighting.
Michael Burry says he covered shorts in MU, NBIS, CAT, SOXX, CRWV, NVDA and PLTR and replaced many with puts, partly for tax-loss harvesting. He says the AI bubble may burst sooner rather than later.
KKR warns AI spending could expose 20% of the investment-grade index to common risk, with nearly $8T of projected AI infrastructure investment by 2030.

Money market funds hold a record $8.44T. ETFs took in over $1.5T in three quarters, above the full-year record. Global money supply hit a record $103.66T, with the Fed, ECB, BoJ and PBOC adding $1T in August, the 10th straight monthly rise.

Ethereum: Vitalik Buterin says next year's Hegota upgrade is likely the last 'normal' one, with later work focused on zero-knowledge proofs and quantum safety. ARK Venture Fund (ARKVX) is being tokenized on Ethereum through Securitize.

sector_views.rationale: Tech outperformed on the week and AI-linked names keep leading a market where non-AI stocks lag.
Financials were a notable laggard on the week.

earnings_insights: Accenture Q4 (reported this week): EPS $3.29 actual vs $3.18 consensus estimate. Margins rose from 11.6% to 15.3% year over year. Shares rose about 20% premarket and 21% on the week.
Micron: $93B of profit in three quarters of 2026 vs $59B over nearly a decade, per a cited social media post (basis not specified).
Nike: falling revenue and layoff plans reported, shares more than 40% lower on the year.

crypto_views: Bitcoin rose above $87,000, its highest since September 23, then gave back gains Friday as real yields spiked. Bitcoin, Nasdaq futures and gold spiked briefly on the weak payrolls print.
Bitcoin ETF cumulative flows are positive year to date, but about $5B short of closing the outflow hole since the October 10 peak.

Vitalik Buterin says Ethereum is 'really not just a blockchain anymore' and that next year's Hegota upgrade is likely the last 'normal' one, followed by work on zero-knowledge proofs and quantum safety. He expects finality as fast as 8 seconds by 2030, vs about 200 seconds in 2015.
ARK Venture Fund (ARKVX), holding OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe and Databricks, is being tokenized on Ethereum through Securitize.
Global money supply at a record $103.66T is cited as supportive for scarce assets.
risk_factors: Sticky inflation with an ISM prices index at 77.9 complicates the policy path even after weak payrolls.
Bond market is pricing a higher cost of capital while AI-heavy equities assume earnings growth can outrun it, and credit is now moving with bonds.
CCC spreads above 1,000bps and wider high-yield spreads signal credit stress spreading beyond the weakest names.
French fiscal and political risk spreading to Italy and weighing on the euro.
Oil and Hormuz risk from the Iran conflict and attacks on tankers.
AI valuation and financing risk: Anthropic's $518B commitments, negative hyperscaler cash flow, and KKR's warning that 20% of the investment-grade index could be exposed.
Bank deposit risk if AI agents sweep household cash into higher-yielding accounts (Apollo's Torsten Slok).
Narrow market leadership and weak breadth beneath record index levels.
Possible IPO delay for Anthropic until after the November midterms.

Analysis cited says Iran is losing its grip on Hormuz as sanctions tighten and may respond by escalating.
G7 agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel stocks in response to Trump's threatened US ban on diesel exports.

tension_points.theme: AI equities vs cost of capital
tension_points.bull_case: AI-heavy equities keep behaving as though earnings growth can outrun higher rates. Accenture, Synopsys and NVDA (17x forward P/E) show strong AI-linked results, and semiconductor free cash flow is above $400B.
tension_points.bear_case: The bond market prices a significantly higher cost of capital and credit is joining it, with high-yield spreads wider and CCCs above 1,000bps. Hyperscaler cash flow is negative and KKR warns of AI debt exposure in 20% of the investment-grade index.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit spreads continuing to widen alongside the bond selloff while equities hold, as the report frames the divergence as unsustainable.

tension_points.bear_case: Inflation is sticky (core PCE 3.0%, ISM prices 77.9) and resilient demand complicates the outlook.
